source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Suspect pulmonary tuberculosis, use appropriate airborne precautions, and arrange prompt TB evaluation","B":"Treat the symptoms as an uncomplicated common cold and postpone additional respiratory evaluation","C":"Assume seasonal allergies despite hemoptysis, prolonged cough, weight loss, and night sweats","D":"Delay diagnostic evaluation until the cough and systemic symptoms persist for several more months"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC lists cough lasting 3 weeks or longer, hemoptysis, chest symptoms, unexplained weight loss, fever, and night sweats among pulmonary TB findings. Healthcare TB infection-control programs should ensure prompt detection and airborne infection-isolation precautions for confirmed or presumptive infectious TB disease.
source_row.source_detail: CDC 2024-2025 clinical guidance: pulmonary TB symptoms include cough ≥3 weeks, hemoptysis, weight loss and night sweats; healthcare settings require prompt detection and airborne infection isolation for confirmed or presumptive infectious TB.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Clinical Overview and Signs/Symptoms of Tuberculosis Disease
source_row.stem: A client has a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, and hemoptysis. What should the nurse do?
